outcomes.text: Choose an available word order for particles, recipients and extraposed subjects.
Use a cleft to highlight the information a reader is looking for.
Identify which clause becomes passive and choose the required complement form.

key_terms.definition: A construction with it in the usual subject position and a clause later, as in It would help to close the valve.
A construction such as It was Maya who closed the valve, which singles out a value for a role.
A specifying construction such as What helped was closing the valve, with a fused relative as one part.
A construction that can make the affected participant the subject, as in The valve was closed by Maya.

options.text: Maya brought them back.
options.feedback: The unstressed object pronoun comes before the particle.

options.text: Maya brought back them.
options.feedback: The unstressed object pronoun comes before the particle.

options.text: Maya them brought back.
options.feedback: The unstressed object pronoun comes before the particle.

opening.prompt: Choose the ordinary particle order when the direct object is unstressed them.

options.text: Maya closed the valve.
options.feedback: The cleft places Maya in the identifying slot before the relative.

options.text: What helped was closing the valve.
options.feedback: The cleft places Maya in the identifying slot before the relative.

options.text: It was Maya who closed the valve.
options.feedback: The cleft places Maya in the identifying slot before the relative.

opening.prompt: Which line specifically answers “Who closed the valve?” with an it-cleft?

options.text: The clause headed by saw
options.feedback: We saw is active. Maya undergoes the splashing in the lower clause.

options.text: The lower splashing clause
options.feedback: We saw is active. Maya undergoes the splashing in the lower clause.

options.text: Both clauses
options.feedback: We saw is active. Maya undergoes the splashing in the lower clause.

opening.prompt: Which clause is passive in “We saw Maya get splashed”?

options.text: Would it help to close the valve?
options.feedback: It goes in the subject position and the infinitival comes later.

options.text: Would the valve close?
options.feedback: It goes in the subject position and the infinitival comes later.

options.text: Would to close the valve help?
options.feedback: It goes in the subject position and the infinitival comes later.

options.text: What helped was closing the valve.
options.feedback: What helped sets up a value, and closing the valve specifies it.

options.text: It was Maya who closed the valve.
options.feedback: What helped sets up a value, and closing the valve specifies it.

options.text: Closing the valve helped.
options.feedback: What helped sets up a value, and closing the valve specifies it.

opening.prompt: Which pseudo-cleft names the action that helped?

options.text: We sent to Jo a reminder.
options.feedback: The direct-object-first wording uses a recipient to phrase.

options.text: We sent a reminder Jo.
options.feedback: The direct-object-first wording uses a recipient to phrase.

options.text: We sent a reminder to Jo.
options.feedback: The direct-object-first wording uses a recipient to phrase.

closing.prompt: Reword “We sent Jo a reminder” so that the reminder comes before Jo.

options.text: I believe it Maya who closed the valve.
options.feedback: The raised-object cleft construction uses be. I believe that it was Maya would use a different frame.

options.text: I believe Maya who closed the valve.
options.feedback: The raised-object cleft construction uses be. I believe that it was Maya would use a different frame.

options.text: I believe it to be Maya who closed the valve.
options.feedback: The raised-object cleft construction uses be. I believe that it was Maya would use a different frame.

closing.prompt: Which wording keeps the raised it-cleft after “I believe”?

options.text: Maya was seen to close the valve.
options.feedback: When see is passive in this frame, to appears before close.

options.text: They saw Maya get splashed.
options.feedback: When see is passive in this frame, to appears before close.

options.text: Maya was seen close the valve.
options.feedback: When see is passive in this frame, to appears before close.

closing.prompt: Make see passive in “They saw Maya close the valve”.

options.text: Who called was Jo.
options.feedback: The one provides an overt head for the relative. The last line uses an embedded question instead.

options.text: I know who called.
options.feedback: The one provides an overt head for the relative. The last line uses an embedded question instead.

options.text: The one who called was Jo.
options.feedback: The one provides an overt head for the relative. The last line uses an embedded question instead.

closing.prompt: Which sentence specifies the identity of the person, using a subject noun phrase with an integrated relative?

options.text: We saw Maya splash water. / We saw Maya run.
options.feedback: Get splashed and the bare splashed by a wave both present Maya as undergoing the event.

options.text: Maya was seen to splash water. / We saw Maya splash water.
options.feedback: Get splashed and the bare splashed by a wave both present Maya as undergoing the event.

options.text: We saw Maya get splashed. / We saw Maya splashed by a wave.
options.feedback: Get splashed and the bare splashed by a wave both present Maya as undergoing the event.

closing.prompt: Which pair keeps see active but makes the lower event passive?
